Question: A digital watch displays hours and minutes with am and pm. What is the largest possible sum of the digits in the display?
Solution:
An am/pm display uses hours \(1\) through \(12\). Among hours \(1\) through \(9\), the largest digit sum is \(9\). The remaining hours, \(10,11,12\), have digit sums \(1,2,3\), so no hour contributes more than \(9\).

Minutes run from \(00\) through \(59\), so their tens digit is at most \(5\) and their ones digit is at most \(9\). Thus the minute digits sum to at most \(14\).

Every display consequently has digit sum at most \(9+14=23\). The valid time \(9{:}59\), either am or pm, attains this bound:
\[
9+5+9=23.
\]
The largest possible sum is \(\boxed{23}\), choice E.
